_comment: Which firmware image each MMDVM board takes. scripts/release_build.sh builds one image per board (<id>.bin) with its Makefile target, and carries these entries into the release's firmware.json with what each image reports and how it can be flashed.
id: the board's name in Pi-Star (Pi-Star 4's pistar-modemupgrade names where it had the board); aliases: other names for the same board and image.

target: the Makefile target (the board's pins and MCU). hse: the MCU crystal in Hz, where it is not the Makefile's default for the target. define / undefine: Config.h options set or cleared for this board (Config.h is otherwise upstream's).

Unlike MMDVM_HS, MMDVM firmware does not name the board in its version string (only the DRCC and Repeater Builder builds do), so Pi-Star asks which board it is, once; what it reports narrows the choice.

flash: the ways the board can be flashed. stm32flash with gpio: on the Pi's serial port, the STM32's BOOT0 and RESET on these Raspberry Pi GPIO lines (BCM). st-flash: through the ST-LINK on the board's own USB. Any STM32 board on a serial port can also be flashed by hand (BOOT0 set, reset pressed): Pi-Star offers that where no other way applies.

Facts taken from Pi-Star 4's images (firmware 20221121): ZUM Radio boards have a 12 MHz MCU crystal (the pi and pi-f722 targets' default) and report NO TCXO; every other board an 8 MHz crystal (the Makefile default). GPIO 20/21 is what Pi-Star 4 used for every repeater board on the Pi header. MMDVM_RPT_Hat 0.2 and 0.3 had separate images in Pi-Star 4, as did Repeater Builder V3 and V4: upstream builds one target for each pair, so each pair shares an image here.
The DRCC boards have no mode LEDs (their pins files have none), so they are built without MODE_LEDS, as Config.h must be for them.
Every Makefile target must be used by a board, so a target added upstream fails the build until it is mapped here.
